overview: This bill, the Countering Wrongful Detention Act of 2025, gives the government new tools to discourage foreign countries from unjustly jailing Americans to use them as bargaining chips. It lets the Secretary of State label a country a "State Sponsor of Unlawful or Wrongful Detention" if Americans are wrongfully held there or its government is involved, publish a list of such countries, and then review possible penalties such as sanctions, visa limits, export restrictions or travel restrictions. It requires airlines and ticket sellers to have travelers to places with State Department warnings for wrongful detention or kidnapping confirm they have read the warning and understand the risks. It also creates an advisory council of former hostages and detainees, their families and experts to advise the government's hostage recovery offices, and requires a report on how those offices could be improved. As of June 18, 2025, a Senate committee had approved it and it was on the Senate calendar for possible floor action.
for: Supporters say naming and penalizing countries that take Americans as political bargaining chips will make detentions more costly and help keep travelers informed and safe.
against: Critics say a public label could make negotiations for detained Americans harder, and the ticket-purchase certification adds a burden on travelers and airlines without much practical effect.
